title: Indian Family Offices Eye Southeast Asia’s Startups
gist: Indian family offices, now over 300 managing more than $30 billion, are shifting from real estate and gold toward startups in healthtech, fintech and AI, increasingly eyeing Southeast Asia; family office-backed startup funding nearly doubled to $1.62 billion in 2024.

insights.claim: India hosts more than 300 family offices managing over $30 billion in assets, according to The Economic Times and 1Lattice.
insights.speaker: Maxwell Abbott
insights.so_what: Sizes a growing private capital pool that can back startups and cross-border deals.
insights.quote: the country now hosts more than 300 family offices managing over $30 billion in assets

insights.claim: Indian high-net-worth families with over $30 million in assets are projected to nearly double from 16,000 in 2025 to 26,000 by 2030.
insights.speaker: Maxwell Abbott
insights.so_what: Signals rapid UHNW wealth formation in India, expanding the wealth-management and private-capital market.
insights.quote: High-net-worth families with more than $30 million in assets are projected to nearly double, from 16,000 in 2025 to 26,000 by 2030

insights.claim: Intergenerational wealth transfer in India is expected to reach $1.3-1.5 trillion over the next decade.
insights.speaker: Maxwell Abbott
insights.so_what: A massive capital handover likely to reshape Indian asset allocation preferences.
insights.quote: intergenerational wealth transfer reaching $1.3-1.5 trillion over the next decade

insights.claim: Over half of Indian family offices now include millennials or Gen Z members in investment decisions.
insights.speaker: Maxwell Abbott
insights.so_what: Younger decision-makers are driving riskier, tech-heavy allocations.
insights.quote: over half of family offices now featuring millennials or Gen Z members in investment decisions

insights.claim: Roughly 30% of Indian family offices now favor startup allocations in healthtech, fintech and AI over traditional real estate and gold.
insights.speaker: Maxwell Abbott
insights.so_what: Implies reduced marginal demand for gold and property from Indian wealthy families and more for venture assets.
insights.quote: roughly 30% now favor startup allocations in healthtech, fintech, and AI, versus traditional investments such as real estate and gold

insights.claim: Family office-backed startup funding in India nearly doubled to $1.62 billion in 2024 from $876.7 million in 2023, per Tracxn data cited by CNA.
insights.speaker: Maxwell Abbott
insights.so_what: Family offices are becoming a meaningful venture funding source for Indian and regional startups.
insights.quote: family office-backed startup funding nearly doubled to $1.62 billion in 2024 from $876.7 million the year before

insights.claim: Analysts say family offices offer 'patient capital' free of the eight-to-ten-year return pressure on institutional VC, making them attractive to founders with long development cycles.
insights.speaker: Maxwell Abbott
insights.so_what: Family-office capital may fill gaps in deep-tech and long-cycle sectors that institutional VC underserves.
insights.quote: funds without the eight-to-ten-year return pressure that constrains institutional VC

insights.claim: Sattva Group's family office diversified from real estate into tech, backing InCred, while Artha India Ventures was an early Oyo investor.
insights.speaker: Maxwell Abbott
insights.so_what: Concrete examples of Indian family offices acting as tech investors.
insights.quote: Cases like Sattva Group’s family office (which diversified from real estate into tech, backing firms like InCred) and Artha India Ventures (an early Oyo investor) illustrate the trend.

insights.claim: Geopolitical volatility has increased the appeal of relationship-led family office capital, but PwC's Falguni Shah notes governance and intrafamily alignment remain key challenges as these offices scale.
insights.speaker: Maxwell Abbott
insights.so_what: Governance weaknesses are a key diligence risk when partnering with scaling family offices.
insights.quote: governance and intrafamily alignment remain key challenges as these offices scale
